newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures finish sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures finish sharply higher.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures settled sharply higher after rallying into the closing bell following the Federal Reserve's decision to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged, traders said.
"We were in fast markets from the time of the Fed announcement to the close," one currency futures floor trader said.
June Swiss francs settled above the key $0.7164 resistance level, which corresponds to 1.40 spot Swiss francs.
"The 1.40 spot level is key," Marc Chandler, senior analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said.
The strength of the Swiss franc was reflected in the cash mark/Swiss franc cross rate.

Cash mark/Swiss francs fell below 82.80 centimes, which Chandler said was a critical level, in late afternoon U.S. dealings. The 82.80 level is a 61.8-percent Fibonacci retracement level of the mark's climb rise from September 1995 to February 1997.

Flight-to-quality buying of Swiss francs continued in U.S. markets as the dollar has widened its losses against most currencies. In overseas trade, the mark/Swiss franc rate sold off to 82.87 centimes, the lowest level since October 1996.
In late U.S. pit trade, June Swiss francs surged to $0.7260, which currently corresponds to 1.3815 spot, while June marks shot up to $0.5975, near resistance at $0.5780 or about 1.6755 spot marks.
Further resistance for June Swiss francs is at $0.7297, or 1.3745 spot, and at $0.7316, which is a 50-percent retracement level from the contract's five-month downmove.
Meanwhile, June sterling rose to $1.66, its highest level since mid-January. The contract had little response to comments made earlier in the day by U.K. Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.
Brown said the new arrangements in the U.K.'s Securities and Investment Board (SIB) could lead to lower long-term interest rates.

And Canadian dollar futures, which had been trading lower for most of the day, reversed direction after the FOMC meeting ended and closed higher. June Canadian dollars rose to $0.7339, above resistance at $0.7317 to $0.7318. Resistance is at $0.7347, the 100-day moving average.
The dollar immediately gave back all its short-covering gains when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) ended its meeting with no rate announcement.
Traders were evenly split on the outcome of the one-day meeting, with a Reuters poll showing that 21 out of 39 primary dealers were looking for no rate hike.
June yen set a fresh session high of $0.008925, but failed to muster momentum to the GLOBEX high of $0.008970.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000221 at $0.008904, marks were up $0.0094 to $0.5962, Swiss francs were up $0.0197 to $0.7227, sterling was up $0.0162 at $1.6558, Canadian dollars were up $0.0021 to $0.7328, Australian dollars fell $0.0008 to $0.7739, and Mexican pesos rose $0.000175 at $0.125550.
